finding.expected: Treat the dispatched TASK id strictly as data, never as PowerShell source. Pass it through a safe environment/argument boundary (and optionally validate the canonical TASK-id shape before invocation) so shell metacharacters cannot create additional commands. Preserve exactly one canonical `aios run` call, the explicit executor choice, persistent-repository binding, no checkout, no retry/fallback, and minimum workflow permissions. Add a deterministic regression using an injection-shaped TASK-id value proving it cannot execute a second shell command.
finding.issue: The workflow interpolates `${{ inputs.task_id }}` directly into a PowerShell `run:` script. `task_id` is a free-form string input, so PowerShell metacharacters in the dispatch value are parsed as shell syntax before AIOS receives the TASK id. An otherwise authorized workflow-dispatch caller can therefore turn the semantic TASK selector into an arbitrary command on the privileged self-hosted runner, bypassing the intended bounded wakeup contract and potentially causing more than the one authorized `aios run` invocation required by AC3.
